stocks.name: Apple
stocks.description: iPhones, Macs and a giant app store. A huge, profitable tech company that tends to move with the market.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.description: Windows, Office and the Azure cloud. Steady subscription income makes it one of the calmer tech giants.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.description: Makes the chips that power AI. Investors love its growth, so the price swings wildly on every bit of news.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.description: Networking and custom AI chips plus business software. A big winner of the data-centre boom.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.description: Databases that run banks and airlines, now racing to rent out AI cloud computing.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.description: Sales and customer-service software, sold by subscription to millions of businesses.

stocks.name: AMD
stocks.description: NVIDIA's main rival in graphics and AI chips. Its price swings hard on every product launch.

stocks.name: Adobe
stocks.description: Photoshop and PDF maker. Investors worry that AI image tools could eat its lunch.

stocks.name: Intel
stocks.description: The old king of PC chips, spending billions to catch up with rivals. A turnaround bet.

stocks.name: Cisco
stocks.description: Routers and switches that carry internet traffic. Mature, steady and pays a dividend.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.description: Google search, YouTube and Android. Advertising pays for almost everything.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.description: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Ad money is huge, and so are its AI and VR bets.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.description: The streaming giant. Subscriber numbers each quarter can move the price a lot.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.description: Theme parks, Marvel, Pixar and Disney+. Does well when families travel and spend.

stocks.name: T-Mobile US
stocks.description: America's fastest-growing phone network. People pay their phone bill in any economy.

stocks.name: Verizon
stocks.description: A big phone and internet provider with heavy debts and a high, steady dividend.

stocks.name: AT&T
stocks.description: Another phone giant. Slow growth and a big dividend: a classic 'income' stock.

stocks.name: Comcast
stocks.description: Cable TV, broadband and NBCUniversal. Losing TV customers but still very profitable.

stocks.name: Electronic Arts
stocks.description: Video games like EA Sports FC and The Sims. A big launch can make or break a quarter.

stocks.name: Take-Two Interactive
stocks.description: Publisher of Grand Theft Auto. Its price waits on huge, rare game releases.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.description: Online shopping plus the AWS cloud. A consumer company that trades with the energy of a tech stock.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.description: Electric cars plus big promises about robots and self-driving. One of the wildest stocks around.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.description: DIY and builder supplies. Sales follow the housing market and home renovations.

stocks.name: McDonald's
stocks.description: Burgers in 100+ countries. People keep eating out cheaply even in tough times.

stocks.name: Nike
stocks.description: Sneakers and sportswear. Fashion trends and sales in China drive the share price.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.description: People buy soft drinks in good times and bad, so this 'defensive' stock is usually calm and slow.

stocks.name: PepsiCo
stocks.description: Pepsi plus snacks like Doritos and Lay's. A calm, defensive consumer stock.

stocks.name: Procter & Gamble
stocks.description: Toothpaste, nappies and washing powder: things people buy every week, boom or bust.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.description: The giant discount supermarket. Shoppers trade down to it when money is tight, which cushions bad times.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.description: Membership warehouse clubs. Loyal shoppers renew every year, so sales are steady.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.description: One of the world's biggest oil companies. Its profits rise and fall with the oil price, not with tech hype.

stocks.name: Chevron
stocks.description: Another oil and gas major. It usually moves together with Exxon because both live off the same oil price.

stocks.name: ConocoPhillips
stocks.description: Pumps oil and gas but owns no refineries, so it feels oil-price swings directly.

stocks.name: EOG Resources
stocks.description: A shale oil driller in Texas. Profits jump when oil is expensive.

stocks.name: Schlumberger
stocks.description: Oilfield services: it does the drilling and testing for oil companies around the world.

stocks.name: Halliburton
stocks.description: Fracking and drilling services. Busy when oil prices are high, quiet when they fall.

stocks.name: Occidental Petroleum
stocks.description: An oil producer famous for Warren Buffett's big stake. Moves hard with crude oil.

stocks.name: Phillips 66
stocks.description: Refines crude oil into petrol and diesel. Earns the gap between oil and fuel prices.

stocks.name: Marathon Petroleum
stocks.description: The biggest US refiner. The summer driving season is its favourite time of year.

stocks.name: Kinder Morgan
stocks.description: Pipelines that carry natural gas, paid like a toll road. Steadier than the oil drillers.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.description: America's biggest bank. Banks do well when the economy is strong and suffer when loans go bad.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.description: A huge consumer bank. Profits rise with interest rates and fall when loans go bad.

stocks.name: Wells Fargo
stocks.description: A big US bank rebuilding its reputation after scandals.

stocks.name: Citigroup
stocks.description: A global bank in the middle of a long restructuring. More volatile than its rivals.

stocks.name: Goldman Sachs
stocks.description: Investment bank and trader. Busy, profitable markets mean big bonuses.

stocks.name: Morgan Stanley
stocks.description: Investment bank and wealth manager for rich clients. Does well when markets rise.

stocks.name: BlackRock
stocks.description: The world's biggest fund manager (iShares ETFs). It earns more as markets go up.

stocks.name: American Express
stocks.description: Premium credit cards. Its customers keep spending on travel and dining.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.description: Takes a tiny cut of billions of card payments. More shopping means more profit.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.description: Visa's twin: a small fee on every card payment, and no loans of its own.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.description: Diabetes and weight-loss drugs have made it the world's most valuable drug company.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.description: America's largest health insurer. Government rule changes can hit it hard.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.description: Medicines and medical devices. People need healthcare in any economy, so it rarely panics with the market.

stocks.name: Merck
stocks.description: Maker of Keytruda, a top cancer drug. When its patents expire, sales could drop.

stocks.name: AbbVie
stocks.description: Immunology drugs like Humira and Skyrizi. Pays a big dividend.

stocks.name: Thermo Fisher
stocks.description: Sells the tools and chemicals every lab uses. Grows with medical research.

stocks.name: Abbott Laboratories
stocks.description: Medical devices, diagnostic tests and baby formula. Steady and diversified.

stocks.name: Amgen
stocks.description: A biotech pioneer with old blockbusters and a new obesity drug in trials.

stocks.name: Pfizer
stocks.description: A drug maker whose price jumps or drops when a big drug trial succeeds or fails.

stocks.name: Moderna
stocks.description: mRNA vaccine maker. One trial result can double or halve the price: very risky.

stocks.name: GE Aerospace
stocks.description: Builds jet engines and earns for decades by servicing them. More flying means more profit.

stocks.name: Caterpillar
stocks.description: Yellow bulldozers and mining trucks. A barometer of global building and mining.

stocks.name: Boeing
stocks.description: Passenger jets and defence. Quality problems have made it a risky turnaround story.

stocks.name: Honeywell
stocks.description: A conglomerate making aircraft parts, building controls and factory software.

stocks.name: UPS
stocks.description: Brown parcel trucks. Parcel volumes rise and fall with online shopping and trade.

stocks.name: Lockheed Martin
stocks.description: F-35 jets and missiles. Paid by governments, so it hardly notices recessions.

stocks.name: RTX
stocks.description: Jet engines (Pratt & Whitney) and missiles: half airline business, half defence.

stocks.name: Deere & Company
stocks.description: Green tractors and farm machines. Farmers buy more when crop prices are high.

stocks.name: Union Pacific
stocks.description: A railroad across the western US hauling coal, grain and containers.

stocks.name: FedEx
stocks.description: Express delivery by plane. Its results are an early warning about the economy.

stocks.name: Linde
stocks.description: Industrial gases like oxygen and hydrogen, sold on long contracts. Very steady.

stocks.name: Sherwin-Williams
stocks.description: Paint for homes and factories. Busy when people buy and renovate houses.

stocks.name: Air Products
stocks.description: Another industrial-gas maker, betting big on clean hydrogen plants.

stocks.name: Ecolab
stocks.description: Cleaning and hygiene products for hotels, hospitals and food factories.

stocks.name: Freeport-McMoRan
stocks.description: One of the biggest copper miners. Copper prices follow the global economy.

stocks.name: Newmont
stocks.description: The largest gold miner. Gold often rises when investors are scared.

stocks.name: Nucor
stocks.description: America's biggest steelmaker. Steel prices boom and bust with construction.

stocks.name: Dow Inc
stocks.description: Plastics and chemicals. Profits are cyclical and depend on cheap natural gas.

stocks.name: DuPont
stocks.description: Specialty materials for electronics, water filters and protective gear.

stocks.name: Albemarle
stocks.description: Lithium for electric-car batteries. When lithium prices crash, so does the stock.

stocks.name: NextEra Energy
stocks.description: The biggest builder of wind and solar farms. Sensitive to interest rates.

stocks.name: Southern Company
stocks.description: Electricity for the US South. Regulated prices make its profits predictable.

stocks.name: Duke Energy
stocks.description: Power for the Carolinas and Florida. A classic sleep-well-at-night dividend stock.

stocks.name: Dominion Energy
stocks.description: Virginia's power company, building a giant offshore wind farm.

stocks.name: American Electric Power
stocks.description: Runs one of the largest power grids in the US. Steady and boring, on purpose.

stocks.name: Exelon
stocks.description: Delivers electricity and gas to cities like Chicago and Philadelphia.

stocks.name: Sempra
stocks.description: California and Texas utilities plus natural-gas export terminals.

stocks.name: Xcel Energy
stocks.description: A Midwest power company leading the switch from coal to wind.

stocks.name: PG&E
stocks.description: California's big utility. Wildfire lawsuits make it far riskier than other utilities.

stocks.name: Consolidated Edison
stocks.description: Keeps New York City's lights on. One of the calmest stocks on the board.

stocks.name: Prologis
stocks.description: Owns warehouses rented to Amazon and other retailers. A bet on online shopping.

stocks.name: American Tower
stocks.description: Owns phone towers and rents space on them to mobile networks.

stocks.name: Equinix
stocks.description: Data centres where internet companies plug into each other. Grows with the cloud.

stocks.name: Welltower
stocks.description: Senior housing and medical buildings. An ageing population is its tailwind.

stocks.name: Simon Property Group
stocks.description: Shopping malls and outlets. Lives or dies by shoppers turning up in person.

stocks.name: Realty Income
stocks.description: Rents buildings to shops and pays its owners a dividend every month.

stocks.name: Public Storage
stocks.description: Self-storage units. People store more when they move house.

stocks.name: Crown Castle
stocks.description: Phone towers and fibre cables. Hurt when interest rates rise.

stocks.name: Digital Realty
stocks.description: Data centres for big tech. AI demand is filling its buildings.

stocks.name: AvalonBay
stocks.description: Owns apartment blocks in big US cities. Rents follow jobs and wages.

etfs.name: Mix-6 ETF
etfs.description: The classic: six companies from three sectors (tech, energy, consumer). Your first diversified fund.

etfs.name: Total Market ETF
etfs.description: All 100 companies, weighted by size like a real index fund. Big companies get big weights, so it leans towards tech.

etfs.name: Tech Leaders ETF
etfs.description: Three tech giants. It is a fund, but all eggs are in one sector: when tech news is bad, everything inside falls together.

etfs.name: Defensive ETF
etfs.description: Drinks, groceries and medicine: things people buy even in a recession. Calmer in crashes, slower in booms.

etfs.name: Tech Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten tech companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad tech news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Communication Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten communication companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad communication news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Consumer Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten consumer companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad consumer news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Energy Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten energy companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad energy news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Finance Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten finance companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad finance news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Healthcare Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten healthcare companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad healthcare news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Industrials Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten industrials companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad industrials news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Materials Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten materials companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad materials news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Utilities Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten utilities companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad utilities news hits the whole fund.

etfs.name: Real Estate Sector ETF
etfs.description: All ten real estate companies, weighted by size. Many companies but only one sector, so one piece of bad real estate news hits the whole fund.
